title: Trace a visitor’s request
where: Your Windows host · lab notebook
expected: Your diagram shows the visitor reaching only the gateway. The gateway can request a page from private IIS. AD and SQL stay outside the DMZ.

title: Choose your practice setup
where: Your Windows host · lab notebook
fields: No Azure compute or gateway bill
expected: Your plan uses four new VMs inside VMware. No Internet publishing or Azure deployment is planned yet.

title: Write down the four networks
where: Windows host · VMware Virtual Network Editor and lab notebook
expected: Your notebook lists four different network ranges and unique addresses. DC01 and DC02 keep their existing settings.

title: Prepare the four new VMs
where: Windows host · Workstation Pro; Linux guest consoles during preparation
command:
sudo dnf upgrade --refresh -y
sudo dnf install -y nginx openssl curl tcpdump open-vm-tools fuse3 policycoreutils-python-utils
sudo systemctl enable --now vmtoolsd
expected: Your new VMs are installed, updated and shut down, ready for the network changes.

title: Create the VMware networks
where: Windows host · VMware Workstation Pro → Edit → Virtual Network Editor
expected: VMnet2, VMnet3, VMnet4 and VMnet5 show Host-only with DHCP off. Only VMnet2 has a host management adapter.

title: Set the Windows host’s management address
where: Windows 10 host · Run → ncpa.cpl
fields: Blank on this virtual management adapter
expected: The Windows host’s VMnet2 adapter shows 10.50.0.254. Its physical Wi-Fi or Ethernet settings have not changed.

title: Connect each VM to the right network
where: Workstation Pro · each powered-off VM → Settings → Network Adapter
expected: FW01 has four adapters with recorded MAC addresses. Each other new VM has just one adapter on the correct VMnet.

title: Install the firewall on FW01
where: FW01 VMware console · OPNsense installer
expected: FW01 starts from its virtual disk. Its four network adapters match the MAC addresses in your notes.

title: Give the firewall its four addresses
where: FW01 console · Set interface IP address
expected: Your Windows host opens the firewall at 10.50.0.1. All four firewall addresses match your plan.

title: Name the firewall connections
where: Windows host browser · FW01 Interfaces
fields: Unchecked for this isolated test network
Review / uncheck only for lab if required
expected: DMZ and APP_PRIVATE are enabled and named correctly. Firewall administration listens only on the private management connection.

title: Keep your administrator access working
where: Windows host browser · Firewall → Aliases, then Rules [new] / interface rules
expected: A fresh browser connection works through ADMIN_TO_FW_HTTPS. The broad LAN rules and automatic anti-lockout rule are disabled.

title: Allow only gateway-to-IIS web requests
where: Windows host browser · Firewall → Rules → DMZ
expected: DMZ_PROXY_TO_IIS_443 sits above DMZ_DENY_OTHER. Other DMZ connections stay blocked; APP_PRIVATE also has its logged deny rule.

title: Set the private IIS server’s name and address
where: IIS-DMZ01 guest console · Windows Server 2019 → ncpa.cpl
expected: IIS-DMZ01 shows IP 10.80.0.40, mask 255.255.255.0 and gateway 10.80.0.1. Its only adapter is VMnet5; it is not a domain controller.

title: Install IIS and open your test page
where: IIS-DMZ01 · Windows PowerShell as Administrator
command:
if ($env:COMPUTERNAME -ne 'IIS-DMZ01') { throw 'Wrong VM. Stop here.' } Install-WindowsFeature Web-Server -IncludeManagementTools Import-Module WebAdministration New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path C:\inetpub\dmz-lab -Force '

Practice DMZ lab

Private IIS backend: IIS-DMZ01

' | Set-Content C:\inetpub\dmz-lab\index.html Stop-Website 'Default Web Site' New-Website -Name 'DMZ-Lab' -PhysicalPath C:\inetpub\dmz-lab -IPAddress 127.0.0.1 -Port 8080 (Invoke-WebRequest http://127.0.0.1:8080 -UseBasicParsing).StatusCode
expected: The local test on IIS-DMZ01 returns your small practice webpage. DMZ-Lab appears in IIS Manager.

title: Add HTTPS to the private website
where: IIS-DMZ01 · elevated PowerShell, then IIS Manager → DMZ-Lab → Bindings
command:
$cert = New-SelfSignedCertificate -DnsName 'iis-backend.lab.example.test' -CertStoreLocation 'Cert:\LocalMachine\My' -FriendlyName 'DMZ-Lab backend' -KeyAlgorithm RSA -KeyLength 3072 -HashAlgorithm SHA256 -NotAfter (Get-Date).AddDays(30)
New-WebBinding -Name 'DMZ-Lab' -Protocol https -IPAddress '10.80.0.40' -Port 443 -HostHeader 'iis-backend.lab.example.test' -SslFlags 1
(Get-WebBinding -Name 'DMZ-Lab' -Protocol https).AddSslCertificate($cert.Thumbprint, 'My')
New-Item -ItemType Directory C:\DMZ-Lab -Force
$pem = '-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----' + "`r`n" + [Convert]::ToBase64String($cert.RawData, [System.Base64FormattingOptions]::InsertLineBreaks) + "`r`n-----END CERTIFICATE-----`r`n"
$pem | Set-Content C:\DMZ-Lab\backend-public.pem -Encoding Ascii
expected: IIS has the HTTPS binding for iis-backend.lab.example.test. backend-public.pem contains the public certificate, with no private key.

title: Limit IIS access and copy its public certificate
where: IIS-DMZ01 · elevated PowerShell; Windows host → Workstation shared folder settings
command:
New-NetFirewallRule -DisplayName 'DMZ-Lab HTTPS from proxy only' -Direction Inbound -Action Allow -Protocol TCP -LocalPort 443 -RemoteAddress 10.60.0.10 -Profile Any
Get-NetFirewallRule -DisplayName 'DMZ-Lab HTTPS from proxy only' | Get-NetFirewallAddressFilter
# Inspect other inbound web allows on this dedicated VM before disabling them.
Get-NetFirewallRule -Direction Inbound -Enabled True -Action Allow | Where-Object DisplayName -Match 'World Wide Web|HTTPS|HTTP' | Select-Object Name,DisplayName,Enabled
expected: Only the gateway IP is allowed through the Windows HTTPS rule. The shared folder contains only the public certificate file.

title: Set the gateway’s DMZ address
where: PROXY01 · AlmaLinux console
command:
sudo hostnamectl set-hostname proxy01.lab.example.test
nmcli connection show
# Replace YOUR_CONNECTION with the exact Ethernet profile name above.
sudo nmcli connection modify "YOUR_CONNECTION" ipv4.method manual ipv4.addresses 10.60.0.10/24 ipv4.gateway 10.60.0.1 ipv4.dns "" ipv6.method disabled
sudo nmcli connection up "YOUR_CONNECTION"
ip -4 address
ip -4 route
timedatectl
expected: PROXY01 shows 10.60.0.10/24 and default gateway 10.60.0.1. No temporary NAT adapter remains.

title: Test the gateway’s connection to IIS
where: PROXY01 · AlmaLinux console; Workstation Options → Shared Folders
command:
sudo mkdir -p /mnt/dmz-transfer
sudo vmhgfs-fuse .host:/DMZ-Transfer /mnt/dmz-transfer -o allow_other
sudo cp /mnt/dmz-transfer/backend-public.pem /etc/pki/tls/certs/iis-backend.pem
curl --cacert /etc/pki/tls/certs/iis-backend.pem --resolve iis-backend.lab.example.test:443:10.80.0.40 --connect-timeout 5 https://iis-backend.lab.example.test/
expected: The gateway receives the IIS practice page with the certificate check enabled. FW01 logs the matching allowed request.

title: Create the gateway’s test certificate
where: PROXY01 · AlmaLinux console
command:
sudo openssl req -x509 -nodes -newkey rsa:3072 -sha256 -days 30 -keyout /etc/pki/tls/private/dmz-front.key -out /etc/pki/tls/certs/dmz-front.crt -subj "/CN=app-dmz.lab.example.test" -addext "subjectAltName=DNS:app-dmz.lab.example.test"
sudo chmod 600 /etc/pki/tls/private/dmz-front.key
openssl x509 -in /etc/pki/tls/certs/dmz-front.crt -noout -subject -dates -ext subjectAltName
sudo cp /etc/pki/tls/certs/dmz-front.crt /mnt/dmz-transfer/proxy-public.crt
expected: The gateway certificate covers app-dmz.lab.example.test and has the expected dates. Only root can read its private key.

title: Copy and check the NGINX configuration
where: PROXY01 · AlmaLinux console / text editor
expected: nginx -t reports that the configuration test succeeded. The settings still verify the private IIS certificate.

title: Start NGINX and keep protections on
where: PROXY01 · AlmaLinux console
command:
sudo setsebool -P httpd_can_network_connect 1
sudo firewall-cmd --get-active-zones
sudo firewall-cmd --permanent --zone=public --add-rich-rule='rule family="ipv4" source address="10.70.0.10/32" service name="https" accept'
sudo firewall-cmd --reload
sudo systemctl enable --now nginx
systemctl is-active nginx
getenforce
sudo ss -lntp | grep ':443'
expected: NGINX is active at 10.60.0.10:443. SELinux and firewalld remain on, with HTTPS allowed only from TEST01.

title: Set the practice visitor’s address
where: TEST01 · AlmaLinux 9 GNOME Settings → Network
command:
sudo hostnamectl set-hostname test01.lab.example.test
ip -4 address
ip -4 route
expected: TEST01 shows 10.70.0.10/24 and gateway 10.70.0.1. Its only VMware adapter is VMnet4.

title: Send visitor HTTPS requests to the gateway
where: Windows host browser · FW01 → Firewall → NAT → Destination NAT / Port Forward
expected: One HTTPS forwarding rule sends the practice visitor to PROXY01. There is no direct outside forward to IIS.

title: Copy the certificate the visitor needs
where: TEST01 · AlmaLinux Terminal; temporary VMware shared folder
command:
mkdir -p ~/dmz-lab
sudo mkdir -p /mnt/dmz-transfer
sudo vmhgfs-fuse .host:/DMZ-Transfer /mnt/dmz-transfer -o allow_other
cp /mnt/dmz-transfer/proxy-public.crt ~/dmz-lab/
openssl x509 -in ~/dmz-lab/proxy-public.crt -noout -fingerprint -sha256
sudo umount /mnt/dmz-transfer
expected: TEST01 has the gateway’s matching public certificate. Shared Folders is now disabled on all practice VMs.

title: Open the page through the full route
where: TEST01 · AlmaLinux Terminal
expected: TEST01 receives the private IIS practice page through PROXY01, with certificate checking enabled.

title: Check that visitors cannot reach IIS directly
where: TEST01 · AlmaLinux Terminal; FW01 Live View
command:
timeout 5 bash -c '</dev/tcp/10.80.0.40/443'
echo "TCP probe exit status: $?"
expected: Direct visitor access to IIS fails with a matching firewall Block. The approved gateway request still works.

title: Check that private management stays blocked
where: PROXY01 · AlmaLinux console; FW01 Live View
expected: The management checks fail with matching Block logs. Gateway-to-IIS HTTPS still works. IIS-to-AD access is also blocked.

title: Save the test results and check the adapters
where: Windows host browser · FW01 Live View and Workstation settings
expected: Your saved checklist has both working and blocked tests, each matched to a log. No extra adapter or shared folder bypass remains.

title: Find the same request in both logs
where: PROXY01 terminal; IIS-DMZ01 → IIS Manager → DMZ-Lab → Logging
expected: You find the same labtrace request in the gateway and IIS logs. IIS sees the gateway as its connecting client.

title: Break and restore one firewall rule
where: Windows host browser · FW01 DMZ rule list; TEST01 terminal
fields: Clear only matching proxy → IIS 443 states
Re-enable rule · Apply · retest both paths
expected: The request fails when the one rule is disabled. It works again after that rule is restored, and your blocked-path tests still fail.

title: Tell certificate and network problems apart
where: PROXY01 · AlmaLinux console
command:
sudo nginx -t
systemctl status nginx --no-pager
getsebool httpd_can_network_connect
openssl x509 -in /etc/pki/tls/certs/iis-backend.pem -noout -subject -dates -ext subjectAltName
sudo tail -n 20 /var/log/nginx/dmz-error.log
expected: You can use the error message to choose the right check: configuration, certificate, clock, service permission or firewall.

title: Practice restoring a working backup
where: Windows host · Workstation consoles and private change notes
expected: Your notes identify the working backup, restore order and test results. DC01 and DC02 were not restored or changed.

where: Your notebook · Azure architecture planning
fields: Application Gateway WAF v2 · dedicated subnet
Private IIS VM · no public IP
expected: Your Azure drawing puts the public gateway and private IIS in separate subnets. The IIS VM has no public IP.

fields: Disks/IP and other services may still bill
expected: Your notes include the region, running hours, estimated charges and deletion plan. No Azure resources were created.

fields: DC01 / DC02 / APP01 / live academy DNS
